1→# Desloppify - an agent harness to make your codebase 🤌
     2→
     3→[![PyPI version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/desloppify)](https://pypi.org/project/desloppify/) ![Python 3.11+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11%2B-blue)
     4→
     5→Desloppify gives your AI coding agent the tools to identify, understand, and systematically improve codebase quality. It combines mechanical detection (dead code, duplication, complexity) with subjective LLM review (naming, abstractions, module boundaries), then works through a prioritized fix loop. State persists across scans so it chips away over multiple sessions, and the scoring is designed to resist gaming.
     6→
     7→<img src="assets/explained.png" width="100%">
     8→
     9→The score gives your agent a north-star, and the tooling helps it plan, execute, and resolve issues until it hits your target — with a lot of tricks to keep it on track. A score above 98 should correlate with a codebase a seasoned engineer would call beautiful.
    10→
    11→That score generates a scorecard badge for your GitHub profile or README:
    12→
    13→<img src="assets/scorecard.png" width="100%">
    14→
    15→Currently supports 28 languages — full plugin depth for TypeScript, Python, C#, Dart, GDScript, and Go; generic linter + tree-sitter support for Rust, Ruby, Java, Kotlin, and 17 more.
    16→
    17→## For your agent's consideration...
    18→
    19→Paste this prompt into your agent:
    20→
    21→```
    22→I want you to improve the quality of this codebase. To do this, install and run desloppify.
    23→Run ALL of the following (requires Python 3.11+):
    24→
    25→pip install --upgrade "desloppify[full]"
    26→desloppify update-skill claude    # installs the full workflow guide — pick yours: claude, cursor, codex, copilot, windsurf, gemini
    27→
    28→Before scanning, check for directories that should be excluded (vendor, build output,
    29→generated code, worktrees, etc.) and exclude obvious ones with `desloppify exclude <path>`.
    30→Share any questionable candidates with me before excluding.
    31→
    32→desloppify scan --path .
    33→desloppify next
    34→
    35→--path is the directory to scan (use "." for the whole project, or "src/" etc).
    36→
    37→Your goal is to get the strict score as high as possible. The scoring resists gaming — the
    38→only way to improve it is to actually make the code better.
    39→
    40→THE LOOP: run `next`. It tells you what to fix, which file, and the resolve command to run
    41→when done. Fix it, resolve it, run `next` again. Over and over. This is your main job.
    42→
    43→Don't be lazy. Large refactors and small detailed fixes — do both with equal energy. No task
    44→is too big or too small. Fix things properly, not minimally.
    45→
    46→Use `plan` to reorder priorities or cluster related issues. Rescan periodically. The scan
    47→output includes agent instructions — follow them, don't substitute your own analysis.
    48→```
    49→
    50→## From Vibe Coding to Vibe Engineering
    51→
    52→Vibe coding gets things built fast. But the codebases it produces tend to rot in ways that are hard to see and harder to fix — not just the mechanical stuff like dead imports, but the structural kind. Abstractions that made sense at first stop making sense. Naming drifts. Error handling is done three different ways. The codebase works, but working in it gets worse over time.
    53→
    54→LLMs are actually good at spotting this now, if you ask them the right questions. That's the core bet here — that an agent with the right framework can hold a codebase to a real standard, the kind that used to require a senior engineer paying close attention over months.
    55→
    56→So we're trying to define what "good" looks like as a score that's actually worth optimizing. Not a lint score you game to 100 by suppressing warnings. Something where improving the number means the codebase genuinely got better. That's hard, and we're not done, but the anti-gaming stuff matters to us a lot — it's the difference between a useful signal and a vanity metric.
    57→
    58→The hope is that anyone can use this to build something a seasoned engineer would look at and respect. That's the bar we're aiming for.
    59→
    60→If you'd like to join a community of vibe engineers who want to build beautiful things, [come hang out](https://discord.gg/aZdzbZrHaY).
    61→
    62→<img src="assets/engineering.png" width="100%">
    63→
    64→---
    65→
    66→Issues, improvements, and PRs are hugely appreciated — [github.com/peteromallet/desloppify](https://github.com/peteromallet/desloppify).
    67→
    68→MIT License
    69→

1→<!-- desloppify-begin -->
     2→<!-- desloppify-skill-version: 3 -->
     3→---
     4→name: desloppify
     5→description: >
     6→  Agent harness for iterative codebase improvement. Use when the user asks
     7→  about code quality, technical debt, dead code, large files, god classes,
     8→  duplicate functions, code smells, naming issues, import cycles, or coupling
     9→  problems. Also use when asked for a health score, what to fix next, or to
    10→  create a cleanup plan. Supports 28 languages.
    11→allowed-tools: Bash(desloppify *)
    12→---
    13→
    14→# Desloppify
    15→
    16→## 1. Your Job
    17→
    18→Maximise the **strict score** honestly. Your main cycle: **scan → plan → execute → rescan**. Follow the scan output's **INSTRUCTIONS FOR AGENTS** — don't substitute your own analysis.
    19→
    20→**Don't be lazy.** Do large refactors and small detailed fixes with equal energy. If it takes touching 20 files, touch 20 files. If it's a one-line change, make it. No task is too big or too small — fix things properly, not minimally.
    21→
    22→## 2. The Workflow
    23→
    24→Three phases, repeated as a cycle.
    25→
    26→### Phase 1: Scan and review — understand the codebase
    27→
    28→```bash
    29→desloppify scan --path .       # analyse the codebase
    30→desloppify status              # check scores — are we at target?
    31→```
    32→
    33→The scan will tell you if subjective dimensions need review. Follow its instructions. To trigger a review manually:
    34→```bash
    35→desloppify review --run-batches --runner codex --parallel --scan-after-import
    36→```
    37→
    38→### Phase 2: Plan — decide what to work on
    39→
    40→After reviews, triage stages and plan creation appear as queue items in `next`. Complete them in order:
    41→```bash
    42→desloppify next                                        # shows the next workflow step
    43→desloppify plan triage --stage observe --report "themes and root causes..."
    44→desloppify plan triage --stage reflect --report "comparison against completed work..."
    45→desloppify plan triage --stage organize --report "summary of priorities..."
    46→desloppify plan triage --complete --strategy "execution plan..."
    47→```
    48→
    49→Then shape the queue. **The plan shapes everything `next` gives you** — don't skip this step.
    50→
    51→```bash
    52→desloppify plan                          # see the full ordered queue
    53→desloppify plan reorder <pat> top        # reorder — what unblocks the most?
    54→desloppify plan cluster create <name>    # group related issues to batch-fix
    55→desloppify plan focus <cluster>          # scope next to one cluster
    56→desloppify plan skip <pat>              # defer — hide from next
    57→```
    58→
    59→More plan commands:
    60→```bash
    61→desloppify plan reorder <cluster> top    # move all cluster members at once
    62→desloppify plan reorder <a> <b> top     # mix clusters + findings in one reorder
    63→desloppify plan reorder <pat> before -t X  # position relative to another item/cluster
    64→desloppify plan cluster reorder a,b top # reorder multiple clusters as one block
    65→desloppify plan resolve <pat>           # mark complete
    66→desloppify plan reopen <pat>             # reopen
    67→```
    68→
    69→### Phase 3: Execute — grind the queue to completion
    70→
    71→Trust the plan and execute. Don't rescan mid-queue — finish the queue first.
    72→
    73→**Branch first.** Create a dedicated branch for health work — never commit directly to main:
    74→```bash
    75→git checkout -b desloppify/code-health    # or desloppify/<focus-area>
    76→```
    77→
    78→**Set up commit tracking.** If you have a PR, link it for auto-updated descriptions:
    79→```bash
    80→desloppify config set commit_pr 42        # PR number for auto-updates
    81→```
    82→
    83→**The loop:**
    84→```
    85→1. desloppify next              ← what to fix next
    86→2. Fix the issue in code
    87→3. Resolve it (next shows you the exact command including required attestation)
    88→4. When you have a logical batch, commit:
    89→   git add <files> && git commit -m "desloppify: fix 3 deferred_import findings"
    90→5. Record the commit:
    91→   desloppify plan commit-log record      # moves findings uncommitted → committed, updates PR
    92→6. Push periodically:
    93→   git push -u origin desloppify/code-health
    94→7. Repeat until the queue is empty
    95→```
    96→
    97→Score may temporarily drop after fixes — cascade effects are normal, keep going.
    98→If `next` suggests an auto-fixer, run `desloppify autofix <fixer> --dry-run` to preview, then apply.
    99→
   100→**When the queue is clear, go back to Phase 1.** New issues will surface, cascades will have resolved, priorities will have shifted. This is the cycle.
   101→
   102→### Other useful commands
   103→
   104→```bash
   105→desloppify next --count 5                         # top 5 priorities
   106→desloppify next --cluster <name>                  # drill into a cluster
   107→desloppify show <pattern>                         # filter by file/detector/ID
   108→desloppify show --status open                     # all open findings
   109→desloppify plan skip --permanent "<id>" --note "reason" --attest "..." # accept debt
   110→desloppify exclude <path>                         # exclude a directory from scanning
   111→desloppify config show                            # show all config including excludes
   112→desloppify scan --path . --reset-subjective       # reset subjective baseline to 0
   113→```
   114→
   115→## 3. Reference
   116→
   117→### How scoring works
   118→
   119→Overall score = **40% mechanical** + **60% subjective**.
   120→
   121→- **Mechanical (40%)**: auto-detected issues — duplication, dead code, smells, unused imports, security. Fixed by changing code and rescanning.
   122→- **Subjective (60%)**: design quality review — naming, error handling, abstractions, clarity. Starts at **0%** until reviewed. The scan will prompt you when a review is needed.
   123→- **Strict score** is the north star: wontfix items count as open. The gap between overall and strict is your wontfix debt.
   124→- **Score types**: overall (lenient), strict (wontfix counts), objective (mechanical only), verified (confirmed fixes only).
   125→
   126→### Subjective reviews in detail
   127→
   128→- **Preferred**: `desloppify review --run-batches --runner codex --parallel --scan-after-import` — does everything in one command.
   129→- **Manual path**: `desloppify review --prepare` → review per dimension → `desloppify review --import file.json`.
   130→- Import first, fix after — import creates tracked state entries for correlation.
   131→- Target-matching scores trigger auto-reset to prevent gaming.
   132→- Even moderate scores (60-80) dramatically improve overall health.
   133→- Stale dimensions auto-surface in `next` — just follow the queue.
   134→
   135→### Review output format
   136→
   137→Return machine-readable JSON for review imports. For `--external-submit`, include `session` from the generated template:
   138→
   139→```json
   140→{
   141→  "session": {
   142→    "id": "<session_id_from_template>",
   143→    "token": "<session_token_from_template>"
   144→  },
   145→  "assessments": {
   146→    "<dimension_from_query>": 0
   147→  },
   148→  "findings": [
   149→    {
   150→      "dimension": "<dimension_from_query>",
   151→      "identifier": "short_id",
   152→      "summary": "one-line defect summary",
   153→      "related_files": ["relative/path/to/file.py"],
   154→      "evidence": ["specific code observation"],
   155→      "suggestion": "concrete fix recommendation",
   156→      "confidence": "high|medium|low"
   157→    }
   158→  ]
   159→}
   160→```
   161→
   162→**Import rules:**
   163→- `findings` MUST match `query.system_prompt` exactly (including `related_files`, `evidence`, and `suggestion`). Use `"findings": []` when no defects found.
   164→- Import is fail-closed: invalid findings abort unless `--allow-partial` is passed.
   165→- Assessment scores are auto-applied from trusted internal or cloud session imports. Legacy `--attested-external` remains supported.
   166→
   167→**Import paths:**
   168→- Robust session flow (recommended): `desloppify review --external-start --external-runner claude` → use generated prompt/template → run printed `--external-submit` command.
   169→- Durable scored import (legacy): `desloppify review --import findings.json --attested-external --attest "I validated this review was completed without awareness of overall score and is unbiased."`
   170→- Findings-only fallback: `desloppify review --import findings.json`
   171→
   172→### Review integrity
   173→
   174→1. Do not use prior chat context, score history, or target-threshold anchoring.
   175→2. Score from evidence only; when mixed, score lower and explain uncertainty.
   176→3. Assess every requested dimension; never drop one. If evidence is weak, score lower.
   177→
   178→### Reviewer agent prompt
   179→
   180→Runners that support agent definitions (Cursor, Copilot, Gemini) can create a dedicated reviewer agent. Use this system prompt:
   181→
   182→```
   183→You are a code quality reviewer. You will be given a codebase path, a set of
   184→dimensions to score, and what each dimension means. Read the code, score each
   185→dimension 0-100 from evidence only, and return JSON in the required format.
   186→Do not anchor to target thresholds. When evidence is mixed, score lower and
   187→explain uncertainty.
   188→```
   189→
   190→See your editor's overlay section below for the agent config format.
   191→
   192→### Commit tracking & branch workflow
   193→
   194→Work on a dedicated branch named `desloppify/<description>` (e.g., `desloppify/code-health`, `desloppify/fix-smells`). Never push health work directly to main.
   195→
   196→```bash
   197→desloppify config set commit_pr 42              # link to your PR
   198→desloppify plan commit-log                      # see uncommitted + committed status
   199→desloppify plan commit-log record               # record HEAD commit, update PR description
   200→desloppify plan commit-log record --note "why"  # with rationale
```

    90→def build_work_queue(
    91→    state: StateModel,

    94→) -> WorkQueueResult:
    95→    """Build a ranked work queue from state findings.
    96→
    97→    Pipeline:
    98→    1. Gather — finding items, subjective dimensions, workflow stages
    99→    2. Score  — estimate impact from dimension headroom, apply floor
   100→    3. Order  — stamp plan positions, sort, filter to cluster focus
   101→    4. Limit  — truncate to count, optionally add explain metadata
   102→    """
   103→    opts = options or QueueBuildOptions()

   105→
   106→    # 1. Gather
   107→    items = build_finding_items(
   108→        state, scan_path=scan_path, status_filter=status,
   109→        scope=opts.scope, chronic=opts.chronic,

   112→    items += _gather_workflow_items(state, plan, status)

   116→    items = [i for i in items if _passes_impact_floor(i)]

   120→    items.sort(key=item_sort_key)

   124→    if not items:

   146→def _resolve_inputs(
   147→    opts: QueueBuildOptions, state: StateModel,
   148→) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None, str, float]:
   149→    """Resolve plan, scan_path, status, and subjective threshold from options."""

   151→    plan = ctx.plan if ctx is not None else opts.plan

   156→        else opts.scan_path  # type: ignore[assignment]

   164→        threshold = float(opts.subjective_threshold)
   165→    except (TypeError, ValueError):

## Terminology Mapping Report: Findings, Issues, Items, and Entries in Desloppify

Based on a thorough search of the desloppify codebase, here's how these terms are used and where they overlap or diverge:

---

### **Canonical Terms (Clear, Consistent Usage)**

#### **"Finding"** — The primary term for a detected problem
- **Location**: Core state model — `state["findings"]` is a dict where keys are finding IDs and values are finding objects
- **Usage scope**: Universal across the codebase
  - Function names: `build_finding_items()`, `is_review_finding()`, `is_subjective_finding()`
  - Docstrings: "Review findings live in state['findings']" (issues.py)
  - User-facing commands: `desloppify show`, `desloppify plan resolve`
  - Output rendering: `render_findings()`, `render_issue_detail()` (confusing, see below)

- **Finding structure** (from `issues_render.py`):
  ```python
  {
    "id": "<finding_id>",
    "detector": "review|concerns|deferred_import|...",
    "confidence": "high|medium|low",
    "summary": "...",
    "file": "path/to/file",
    "status": "open|fixed|wontfix|false_positive|auto_resolved",
    "detail": {
      "dimension": "...",
      "holistic": bool,
      "evidence": [...],
      "suggestion": "...",
      "investigation": "...",
    }
  }
  ```

- **Key insight**: Even review-sourced findings (detector="review") are stored in `findings` dict, not separately.

---

#### **"Item"** — A work-queue element
- **Location**: Work queue API (`build_work_queue()`, queue ranking/rendering)
- **Scope**: Everything that appears in `desloppify next`
- **Types** (via `item["kind"]`):
  - `"finding"` — a finding converted to a queue item
  - `"subjective_dimension"` — a dimension needing review
  - `"cluster"` — a grouped set of findings
  - `"workflow_stage"` — a triage planning stage
  - `"workflow_action"` — a synthetic action (create-plan, import-scores, etc.)

- **Key insight**: An "item" is what the queue builder produces from findings + synthetic work. Items wrap findings and add plan metadata (position, cluster, etc.).

- **From ranking.py docs**:
  ```python
  item = dict(finding)  # Copy finding dict
  item["id"] = finding_id
  item["kind"] = "finding"   # Mark it as a finding item
  item["is_review"] = is_review_finding(item)
  item["is_subjective"] = is_subjective_finding(item)
  ```

---

#### **"Issue"** — Only used in dimension/scoring context
- **Location**: Dimension-level aggregate metrics, NOT individual problems
- **Where it appears**:
  - `dimension_scores[<name>]["issues"]` — count of failing checks in that dimension
  - CLI output: `"(5 of 100 checks failing)"` — where "issues" = count of checks that are "open" (failing)
  - Rendering: `f"({dimension_score['issues']} of {dimension_score['checks']:,} checks failing)"`
  
- **Key distinction**: 
  - A **finding** is an individual problem (e.g., one unused import)
  - An **issue** is a failing check in a dimension (e.g., "checks that don't pass")
  - One detector run produces multiple checks; some checks fail (become issues)

- **From scoring.py (line 231)**:
  ```python
  state["dimension_scores"][name] = {
    "checks": lenient_scores[name]["checks"],      # Total checks in dimension
    "issues": lenient_scores[name]["issues"],      # Checks that failed/are open
    "score": lenient_scores[name]["score"],        # Percentage: (checks - issues) / checks
  }
  ```

---

#### **"Entry"** — Used only in health breakdown / scoring results
- **Location**: `health.py` — `compute_health_breakdown()` returns `entries` array
- **Scope**: Summary-level reporting (status output, scorecards)
- **Structure**:
  ```python
  {
    "name": "<dimension_name>",
    "pool": "mechanical|subjective",
    "score": 85.3,
    "checks": 120,
    "issues": 18,
    "overall_per_point": 0.042,  # How many points this dimension contributes to overall score
    "overall_drag": 0.756,        # Points lost due to failures
    "configured_weight": 1.0,
    "effective_weight": 0.95,
    "pool_share": 0.15,
  }
  ```

- **Key insight**: "Entry" is never user-facing; it's an internal aggregation for building healthscores and reporting tables.

---

### **Confusing Terminology (Overlaps & Muddles)**

#### **"Issues" vs "Findings" — The Main Blur**
The file `issues_render.py` is misnamed:
- It contains functions for rendering **findings** (not issues), e.g., `render_issue_detail(finding: dict)` 
- The module docstring says "Rendering and scoring helpers for **finding** work orders"
- But it's named `issues_render.py` for historical reasons

The function `list_open_review_findings()` lives in `_work_queue/issues.py`, reinforcing the confusion.

**Best practice**: "Finding" is the correct term for an individual problem; "issue" refers only to failing checks in a dimension's aggregate score.

---

#### **"Review Findings" vs "Review Issues"**
- **Review findings** = findings with `detector="review"` (from LLM subjective review)
- These are stored in `state["findings"]` like mechanical findings
- Not called "review issues" anywhere officially, but code calls them "review findings" consistently
- When a review happens, it produces new **findings** that populate `state["findings"]`

---

### **Rarely Used / Deprecated Terms**

#### **"Defect"**
- Used only in review prompt templates and documentation
- Example: `"IMPORTANT: findings must be defects only — never positive observations."`
- Not used in code variable names or APIs

#### **"Violation"**
- Appears only in detector metadata; not a primary term
- Detectors can have a `display` field like "import cycle violation"

---

### **State Model Key Paths**

For reference:
| Path | Contents | Type |
|------|----------|------|
| `state["findings"]` | All mechanical + review findings | `dict[str, dict]` |
| `state["dimension_scores"]` | Aggregated scores per dimension | `dict[str, dict]` with `issues`, `checks`, `score` |
| `state["subjective_assessments"]` | Subjective review scores | `dict[str, float]` |
| `state["potentials"]` | Pre-scoring check counts | Internal working data |
| Work queue | Ranked list of findings + synthetic items | `list[dict]` with `kind` field |

---

### **Summary: What to Use Where**

| Context | Correct Term | Example |
|---------|--------------|---------|
| Individual problem in code | **Finding** | `desloppify show <finding_id>` |
| Check that didn't pass | **Issue** | "3 issues in naming dimension" |
| Work queue element | **Item** | `item["kind"]` = "finding", "cluster", "workflow_stage" |
| Aggregated scoring report | **Entry** | "entries" in health breakdown |
| Something to fix | **Finding** (or **Item**) | "fix the finding" / "work the item queue" |

---

### **Recommendations**

1. **Rename `issues_render.py`** to `findings_render.py` for clarity
2. **Rename module `_work_queue/issues.py`** to `_work_queue/review_findings.py` (since it handles review findings specifically)
3. **In user-facing output**: Always say "finding" for individual problems; say "checks" or "failing checks" when discussing dimension metrics, not "issues"
4. **Documentation**: Add a glossary clarifying:
   - Finding = individual problem (mechanical or review-sourced)
   - Issue = a failing check (metric within dimension scoring)
   - Item = work queue element (finding + metadata)
   - Entry = health aggregation row (reporting only)

1→"""State-backed work queue for review findings.
     2→
     3→Review findings live in state["findings"]. This module provides:
     4→- Listing/sorting open review findings by impact
     5→- Storing investigation notes on findings
     6→- Expiring stale holistic findings during scan
     7→"""
     8→
     9→from __future__ import annotations
    10→
    11→import logging
    12→from datetime import UTC, datetime
    13→
    14→from desloppify.core.issues_render import finding_weight
    15→from desloppify.engine._work_queue.helpers import detail_dict
    16→
    17→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    18→
    19→__all__ = [
    20→    "impact_label",
    21→    "list_open_review_findings",
    22→    "update_investigation",
    23→    "expire_stale_holistic",
    24→]
    25→
    26→
    27→def impact_label(weight: float) -> str:
    28→    """Convert weight to a human-readable impact label."""
    29→    try:
    30→        numeric = float(weight)
    31→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
    32→        return "+"
    33→    if numeric >= 8:
    34→        return "+++"
    35→    if numeric >= 5:
    36→        return "++"
    37→    return "+"
    38→
    39→
    40→def list_open_review_findings(state: dict) -> list[dict]:
    41→    """Return open review findings sorted by impact (highest first)."""
    42→    findings = state.get("findings", {})
    43→    review = [
    44→        finding
    45→        for finding in findings.values()
    46→        if finding.get("status") == "open" and finding.get("detector") == "review"
    47→    ]
    48→
    49→    def _sort_key(finding: dict) -> tuple[float, str]:
    50→        weight, _impact, finding_id = finding_weight(finding)
    51→        return (-weight, finding_id)
    52→
    53→    review.sort(key=_sort_key)
    54→    return review
    55→
    56→
    57→def update_investigation(state: dict, finding_id: str, text: str) -> bool:
    58→    """Store investigation text on a finding. Returns False if not found/not open."""
    59→    finding = state.get("findings", {}).get(finding_id)
    60→    if not finding or finding.get("status") != "open":
    61→        return False
    62→    detail = detail_dict(finding)
    63→    if not detail:
    64→        detail = {}
    65→        finding["detail"] = detail
    66→    detail["investigation"] = text
    67→    detail["investigated_at"] = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
    68→    return True
    69→
    70→
    71→def expire_stale_holistic(state: dict, max_age_days: int = 30) -> list[str]:
    72→    """Auto-resolve holistic review findings older than max_age_days."""
    73→    now = datetime.now(UTC)
    74→    expired: list[str] = []
    75→
    76→    for finding_id, finding in state.get("findings", {}).items():
    77→        if finding.get("detector") != "review":
    78→            continue
    79→        if finding.get("status") != "open":
    80→            continue
    81→        if not detail_dict(finding).get("holistic"):
    82→            continue
    83→
    84→        last_seen = finding.get("last_seen")
    85→        if not last_seen:
    86→            continue
    87→
    88→        try:
    89→            seen_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(last_seen)
    90→        except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
    91→            logger.debug(
    92→                "Skipping holistic finding %s with invalid last_seen %r: %s",
    93→                finding_id,
    94→                last_seen,
    95→                exc,
    96→            )
    97→            continue
    98→
    99→        age_days = (now - seen_dt).days
   100→        if age_days > max_age_days:
   101→            finding["status"] = "auto_resolved"
   102→            finding["resolved_at"] = now.isoformat()
   103→            finding["note"] = "holistic review expired — re-run review to re-evaluate"
   104→            expired.append(finding_id)
   105→
   106→    return expired
   107→

1→"""Shared finding-merge primitives.
     2→
     3→Both ``app/commands/review/merge.py`` (post-import CLI) and
     4→``app/commands/review/batch_core.py`` (batch accumulation) need the same
     5→dedup-and-merge mechanics.  Extracting them here prevents drift.
     6→"""
     7→
     8→from __future__ import annotations
     9→
    10→from collections.abc import Sequence
    11→
    12→
    13→def normalize_word_set(text: str) -> set[str]:
    14→    """Tokenize *text* into lowercase words >= 3 chars."""
    15→    words = "".join(ch.lower() if ch.isalnum() else " " for ch in text).split()
    16→    return {word for word in words if len(word) >= 3}
    17→
    18→
    19→def merge_list_fields(
    20→    target: dict, source: dict, fields: Sequence[str]
    21→) -> None:
    22→    """Deduplicated merge of list *fields* from *source* into *target*."""
    23→    for field in fields:
    24→        merged: list[str] = []
    25→        seen: set[str] = set()
    26→        for src in (target.get(field), source.get(field)):
    27→            if not isinstance(src, list):
    28→                continue
    29→            for item in src:
    30→                value = str(item).strip()
    31→                if not value or value in seen:
    32→                    continue
    33→                seen.add(value)
    34→                merged.append(value)
    35→        if merged:
    36→            target[field] = merged
    37→
    38→
    39→def pick_longer_text(target: dict, source: dict, field: str) -> None:
    40→    """Keep the longer text value for a string *field*."""
    41→    target_text = str(target.get(field, "")).strip()
    42→    source_text = str(source.get(field, "")).strip()
    43→    if len(source_text) > len(target_text):
    44→        target[field] = source_text
    45→
    46→
    47→def track_merged_from(target: dict, source_id: str) -> None:
    48→    """Append *source_id* to ``target['merged_from']`` if not already present."""
    49→    merged_from = target.get("merged_from")
    50→    if not isinstance(merged_from, list):
    51→        merged_from = []
    52→    if source_id and source_id not in merged_from:
    53→        merged_from.append(source_id)
    54→    if merged_from:
    55→        target["merged_from"] = merged_from
    56→

1→"""State scoring, statistics, and suppression accounting."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from copy import deepcopy
     6→
     7→__all__ = [
     8→    "suppression_metrics",
     9→]
    10→
    11→from desloppify.core.enums import finding_status_tokens
    12→from desloppify.engine._scoring.policy.core import matches_target_score
    13→from desloppify.engine._state.filtering import path_scoped_findings
    14→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import StateModel, ensure_state_defaults
    15→from desloppify.engine._state.scoring_coverage import (
    16→    apply_scan_coverage_to_dimension_scores,
    17→)
    18→
    19→_EMPTY_COUNTERS = tuple(sorted(finding_status_tokens()))
    20→_SUBJECTIVE_TARGET_RESET_THRESHOLD = 2
    21→
    22→
    23→def _resolve_lang_from_state(state: StateModel) -> str | None:
    24→    """Best-effort language detection from state (scan_history > lang_capabilities)."""
    25→    history = state.get("scan_history")
    26→    if isinstance(history, list):
    27→        for entry in reversed(history):
    28→            if isinstance(entry, dict):
    29→                lang = entry.get("lang")
    30→                if isinstance(lang, str) and lang.strip():
    31→                    return lang.strip().lower()
    32→    capabilities = state.get("lang_capabilities")
    33→    if isinstance(capabilities, dict) and len(capabilities) == 1:
    34→        only_lang = next(iter(capabilities.keys()))
    35→        if isinstance(only_lang, str) and only_lang.strip():
    36→            return only_lang.strip().lower()
    37→    return None
    38→
    39→
    40→def _count_findings(findings: dict) -> tuple[dict[str, int], dict[int, dict[str, int]]]:
    41→    """Tally per-status counters and per-tier breakdowns."""
    42→    counters = dict.fromkeys(_EMPTY_COUNTERS, 0)
    43→    tier_stats: dict[int, dict[str, int]] = {}
    44→
    45→    for finding in findings.values():
    46→        if finding.get("suppressed"):
    47→            continue
    48→        status = finding["status"]
    49→        tier = finding.get("tier", 3)
    50→        counters[status] = counters.get(status, 0) + 1
    51→        tier_counter = tier_stats.setdefault(tier, dict.fromkeys(_EMPTY_COUNTERS, 0))
    52→        tier_counter[status] = tier_counter.get(status, 0) + 1
    53→
    54→    return counters, tier_stats
    55→
    56→
    57→def _coerce_subjective_score(value: dict | float | int | str | None) -> float:
    58→    """Normalize a subjective assessment score payload to a 0-100 float."""
    59→    raw = value.get("score", 0) if isinstance(value, dict) else value
    60→    try:
    61→        score = float(raw)
    62→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
    63→        score = 0.0
    64→    return max(0.0, min(100.0, score))
    65→
    66→
    67→def _subjective_target_matches(
    68→    subjective_assessments: dict, *, target: float
    69→) -> list[str]:
    70→    """Return dimension keys whose subjective score matches the target band."""
    71→    matches = [
    72→        dimension
    73→        for dimension, payload in subjective_assessments.items()
    74→        if matches_target_score(_coerce_subjective_score(payload), target)
    75→    ]
    76→    return sorted(matches)
    77→
    78→
    79→def _subjective_integrity_baseline(target: float | None) -> dict[str, object]:
    80→    """Create baseline subjective-integrity metadata for scan/reporting output."""
    81→    return {
    82→        "status": "disabled" if target is None else "pass",
    83→        "target_score": None if target is None else round(float(target), 2),
    84→        "matched_count": 0,
    85→        "matched_dimensions": [],
    86→        "reset_dimensions": [],
    87→    }
    88→
    89→
    90→def _apply_subjective_integrity_policy(
    91→    subjective_assessments: dict,
    92→    *,
    93→    target: float,
    94→) -> tuple[dict, dict[str, object]]:
    95→    """Apply anti-gaming penalties for subjective scores clustered on the target."""
    96→    normalized_target = max(0.0, min(100.0, float(target)))
    97→    matched_dimensions = _subjective_target_matches(
    98→        subjective_assessments,
    99→        target=normalized_target,
   100→    )

    14→def finding_weight(finding: dict) -> tuple[float, float, str]:
    15→    """Compute (weight, impact_pts, finding_id) for a finding."""
    16→    confidence = finding.get("confidence", "low")
    17→    is_holistic = finding.get("detail", {}).get("holistic", False)
    18→
    19→    weight = CONFIDENCE_WEIGHTS.get(confidence, 0.3)
    20→    if is_holistic:
    21→        weight *= HOLISTIC_MULTIPLIER
    22→
    23→    return weight, weight, finding.get("id", "")

    26→def _append_assessment_context(

    28→) -> None:
    29→    if not subjective_assessments:
    30→        return
    31→
    32→    detail = finding.get("detail", {})

    45→    lines.append(

    59→    evidence_lines = detail.get("evidence_lines", [])

    87→def _append_investigation(lines: list[str], finding_id: str, detail: dict) -> bool:

   144→def render_issue_detail(
   145→    finding: dict,
   146→    lang_name: str,
   147→    number: int | None = None,
   148→    subjective_assessments: dict | None = None,
   149→) -> str:
   150→    """Render one finding as a markdown work order from state."""
   151→    finding_id = finding["id"]
   152→    detail = finding.get("detail", {})
   153→    detector = finding.get("detector", "")
   154→    is_holistic = detail.get("holistic", False)
   155→    is_review = detector in ("review", "concerns")
   156→
   157→    # Derive dimension: from detail for review, from registry for mechanical.
   158→    raw_dimension = detail.get("dimension", "")
   159→    if raw_dimension:
   160→        dimension = raw_dimension.replace("_", " ")
   161→    else:
   162→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   163→        dimension = meta.dimension.replace("_", " ") if meta else "unknown"
   164→
   165→    confidence = finding.get("confidence", "low")
   166→
   167→    parts = finding_id.split("::")
   168→    identifier = parts[-2] if len(parts) >= 3 else finding.get("file", "unknown")
   169→    weight, impact_pts, _ = finding_weight(finding)
   170→    label = "+++" if weight >= 8 else "++" if weight >= 5 else "+"
   171→
   172→    lines: list[str] = []
   173→    lines.append(f"# {dimension}: {identifier}\n")
   174→    lines.append(f"**Finding**: `{finding_id}`  ")
   175→    if not is_review:
   176→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   177→        detector_display = meta.display if meta else detector
   178→        lines.append(f"**Detector**: {detector_display} | **Confidence**: {confidence}  ")
   179→    else:
   180→        lines.append(f"**Dimension**: {dimension} | **Confidence**: {confidence}  ")
   181→    lines.append(f"**Score impact**: {label} (~{impact_pts:.1f} pts)\n")
   182→
   183→    _append_assessment_context(lines, finding, subjective_assessments)
   184→
   185→    lines.append("## Problem\n")
   186→    lines.append(f"{finding.get('summary', '')}\n")
   187→
   188→    _append_evidence(lines, detail)
   189→
   190→    suggestion = detail.get("suggestion", "")
   191→    if suggestion:
   192→        lines.append("## Suggested Fix\n")
   193→        lines.append(f"{suggestion}\n")
   194→
   195→    _append_files(lines, finding, detail, is_holistic)
   196→
   197→    reasoning = detail.get("reasoning", "")
   198→    if reasoning:
   199→        lines.append("## Why This Matters\n")
   200→        lines.append(f"{reasoning}\n")
   201→
   202→    has_investigation = _append_investigation(lines, finding_id, detail)

   206→        lang_name=lang_name,
   207→        finding_id=finding_id,
   208→        number=number,
   209→    )
   210→    return "\n".join(lines)

     9→def find_suspect_detectors(
    10→    existing: dict,
    11→    current_by_detector: dict[str, int],
    12→    force_resolve: bool,
    13→    ran_detectors: set[str] | None = None,
    14→) -> set[str]:
    15→    """Detectors that had open findings but likely did not actually run this scan."""
    16→    if force_resolve:
    17→        return set()
    18→
    19→    previous_open_by_detector: dict[str, int] = {}
    20→    for finding in existing.values():
    21→        if finding["status"] != "open":
    22→            continue
    23→        detector = finding.get("detector", "unknown")
    24→        previous_open_by_detector[detector] = (
    25→            previous_open_by_detector.get(detector, 0) + 1
    26→        )
    27→
    28→    # 'review' findings enter via `desloppify review --import`, not via scan phases.
    29→    # They are always marked suspect so the scan never auto-resolves them.
    30→    import_only_detectors = {"review"}
    31→    suspect: set[str] = set()
    32→
    33→    for detector, previous_count in previous_open_by_detector.items():
    34→        if detector in import_only_detectors:
    35→            suspect.add(detector)
    36→            continue
    37→        if current_by_detector.get(detector, 0) > 0:
    38→            continue
    39→        if ran_detectors is not None:
    40→            if detector not in ran_detectors:
    41→                suspect.add(detector)
    42→            continue
    43→        if previous_count >= 3:
    44→            suspect.add(detector)
    45→
    46→    return suspect

1→# Desloppify — Technical Internals
     2→
     3→Desloppify is an agent harness that drives iterative codebase improvement. It combines mechanical detection (dead code, smells, coupling) with **subjective analysis**: structured LLM prompts about architecture, design quality, and convention consistency, tracked as scored findings. The score weights subjective findings heavily because that's what actually moves the needle. See the top-level README for philosophy and usage.
     4→
     5→## Directory Layout
     6→
     7→```
     8→desloppify/
     9→├── cli.py              # Argparse, main()
    10→├── state.py            # Persistent-state facade
    11→├── utils.py            # File discovery, path helpers
    12→├── hook_registry.py    # Detector-safe language hook registry
    13→├── app/                # CLI layer (commands, parser, output)
    14→├── engine/             # Scan/scoring/state internals
    15→│   ├── detectors/      # Generic algorithms (zero language knowledge)
    16→│   ├── planning/       # Prioritization and plan generation
    17→│   ├── policy/         # Zones, scoring policy
    18→│   ├── _scoring/
    19→│   ├── _state/
    20→│   └── _work_queue/
    21→├── intelligence/       # Subjective/narrative/review layer
    22→│   ├── narrative/
    23→│   ├── integrity/
    24→│   └── review/
    25→└── languages/          # Language plugins (auto-discovered, see languages/README.md)
    26→    ├── _framework/     # Shared plugin framework, generic_lang(), tree-sitter
    27→    ├── python/         # Full plugins (custom detectors, fixers, review dims)
    28→    ├── typescript/
    29→    ├── csharp/, dart/, gdscript/, go/
    30→    └── rust/, ruby/, java/, ... (22 generic plugins)
    31→```
    32→
    33→## Architecture
    34→
    35→```
    36→Layer 1: engine/detectors/       Generic algorithms. Data-in, data-out. Zero language imports.
    37→Layer 2: languages/_framework/   Shared contracts/helpers. Normalize raw results → tiered findings.
    38→Layer 3: languages/<name>/       Language config + phases + extractors + detectors + fixers.
    39→```
    40→
    41→**Import direction**: `languages/` → `engine/detectors/`. Never the reverse. Detectors needing language-specific behavior use `hook_registry.get_lang_hook(...)`.
    42→
    43→## Data Flow
    44→
    45→```
    46→scan:    LangConfig → LangRun(phases) → generate_findings() → merge_scan() → state-{lang}.json
    47→fix:     LangConfig.fixers → fixer.fix() → resolve in state
    48→detect:  LangConfig.detect_commands[name](args) → display
    49→```
    50→
    51→## Contracts
    52→
    53→**Detector**: `detect_*(data, config) → list[dict]` — generic algorithm, no language assumptions.
    54→
    55→**Phase runner**: `_phase_*(path, lang) → (list[Finding], dict[str, int])` — thin orchestrator calling extractors → generic algorithms → normalization.
    56→
    57→**LangConfig**: Static language contract. Owns phases, detectors, thresholds, hooks.
    58→
    59→**LangRun**: Per-invocation runtime wrapper (`_framework/runtime.py`) carrying mutable state (zone_map, dep_graph, complexity_map). Phases execute against LangRun, not LangConfig.
    60→
    61→## Rules
    62→
    63→- Entry command modules stay thin — behavioral logic in delegated modules
    64→- Dynamic imports only in `languages/__init__.py` (discovery) and `hook_registry.py` (hooks)
    65→- Persistent schema owned by `state.py` + `engine/_state/`. Command modules don't introduce ad-hoc persisted fields
    66→- `LangRun` owns per-run mutable state, not `LangConfig`
    67→
    68→## Non-Obvious Behavior
    69→
    70→- **State scoping**: `merge_scan` only auto-resolves findings matching the scan's `lang` and `scan_path`. A Python scan never touches TS state.
    71→- **Suspect guard**: If a detector drops from >=5 findings to 0, disappearances are held (bypass: `--force-resolve`).
    72→- **Scoring**: Weighted by tier (T4=4x, T1=1x). Strict score penalizes both open and wontfix.
    73→- **Cascade effects**: Fixing one category (e.g. unused imports) can surface work for the next (unused vars). Score can temporarily drop.
    74→- **Tree-sitter optional**: All tree-sitter features degrade gracefully. Without `tree-sitter-language-pack`, generic plugins fall back to tool-only mode.
    75→- **Bandit optional for Python depth**: Without `bandit`, Python-specific security checks are skipped; scan surfaces preflight/post-scan coverage warnings and marks score confidence reduced for security.
    76→
```

    14→ALL_STATUSES = set(issue_status_tokens(include_all=True))
    15→ACTION_TYPE_PRIORITY = {"auto_fix": 0, "refactor": 1, "manual_fix": 2, "reorganize": 3}

    22→def detail_dict(item: dict) -> dict:
    23→    """Return issue detail as a dict; tolerate legacy/non-dict payloads."""
    24→    detail = item.get("detail")
    25→    return detail if isinstance(detail, dict) else {}
    26→
    27→
    28→def status_matches(item_status: str, status_filter: str) -> bool:
    29→    return status_filter == "all" or item_status == status_filter
    30→
    31→
    32→def is_subjective_issue(item: dict) -> bool:
    33→    detector = item.get("detector")
    34→    if detector in {"subjective_assessment"}:
    35→        return True
    36→    if detector == "holistic_review":
    37→        return True
    38→    return False

    40→

    43→
    44→
    45→def is_subjective_queue_item(item: dict) -> bool:
    46→    """True for subjective work items, including collapsed subjective clusters."""
    47→    if item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension":
    48→        return True
    49→    if item.get("kind") == "cluster":
    50→        members = item.get("members", [])
    51→        return bool(members) and all(
    52→            m.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension" for m in members
    53→        )
    54→    return False

    58→    """Return review issue weight aligned with issues list ordering."""
    59→    confidence = str(item.get("confidence", "low")).lower()
    60→    weight_by_confidence = {

    73→    if not scope:

    83→    if "*" in scope:

    88→
    89→    if "::" in scope:

    99→
   100→    # Hash suffix: 8+ hex chars matches the tail segment of a issue ID.

   116→    """Return supported fixers for an item's language when known."""
   117→    lang = str(item.get("lang", "") or "").strip()

    35→def enrich_with_impact(items: list[dict], dimension_scores: dict) -> None:
    36→    """Stamp ``estimated_impact`` on each item based on dimension-level headroom.
    37→
    38→    Impact = ``overall_per_point * headroom`` where headroom = ``100 - score``.
    39→    Items in dimensions with more score headroom sort first.
    40→    """
    41→    if not dimension_scores:
    42→        for item in items:
    43→            item["estimated_impact"] = 0.0
    44→        return
    45→
    46→    from desloppify.engine._scoring.results.health import compute_health_breakdown
    47→    from desloppify.engine._scoring.results.impact import get_dimension_for_detector
    48→
    49→    breakdown = compute_health_breakdown(dimension_scores)
    50→    entries = breakdown.get("entries", [])
    51→
    52→    # Build lookup: normalized dimension name -> {per_point, headroom}
    53→    dim_impact: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
    54→    for entry in entries:
    55→        name = str(entry.get("name", "")).strip()
    56→        if not name:
    57→            continue
    58→        per_point = float(entry.get("overall_per_point", 0.0))
    59→        score = float(entry.get("score", 0.0))
    60→        headroom = 100.0 - score
    61→        dim_impact[name.lower()] = {"per_point": per_point, "headroom": headroom}
    62→
    63→    for item in items:
    64→        impact = _compute_item_impact(item, dim_impact, get_dimension_for_detector)
    65→        item["estimated_impact"] = impact
    66→
    67→
    68→def _compute_item_impact(
    69→    item: dict,
    70→    dim_impact: dict[str, dict[str, float]],
    71→    get_dimension_for_detector,
    72→) -> float:
    73→    """Compute impact value for a single queue item."""
    74→    kind = item.get("kind", "issue")
    75→
    76→    # Subjective items (synthetic dimensions or subjective issues):
    77→    # look up by detail.dimension_name
    78→    if kind == "subjective_dimension" or item.get("is_subjective"):
    79→        dim_name = detail_dict(item).get("dimension_name", "")
    80→        entry = dim_impact.get(dim_name.lower())
    81→        if entry:
    82→            return entry["per_point"] * entry["headroom"]
    83→        return 0.0
    84→
    85→    # Mechanical issues: use detector -> dimension mapping
    86→    detector = item.get("detector", "")
    87→    if detector:
    88→        dimension = get_dimension_for_detector(detector)
    89→        if dimension:
    90→            entry = dim_impact.get(dimension.name.lower())
    91→            if entry:
    92→                return entry["per_point"] * entry["headroom"]
    93→
    94→    return 0.0
    95→

   100→        return float(detail.get("strict_score", item.get("subjective_score", 100.0)))
   101→    return float(item.get("subjective_score", 100.0))

   121→        if chronic and not (

   131→            finding_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(issue.get("confidence", "low"), 9)

   165→def _natural_sort_key(item: dict) -> tuple:
   166→    """Compute natural (non-plan-aware) ranking for queue items."""
   167→    kind = item.get("kind", "issue")
   168→
   169→    # Initial-review subjective items: highest priority
   170→    if kind == "subjective_dimension" and item.get("initial_review"):
   171→        return (_RANK_INITIAL_REVIEW, 0, subjective_score_value(item), item.get("id", ""))
   172→
   173→    # Triage stage items: stage order, blocked after unblocked
   174→    if kind == "workflow_stage":
   175→        blocked_penalty = 1 if item.get("is_blocked") else 0
   176→        stage_index = int(item.get("stage_index", 0))
   177→        return (_RANK_TRIAGE_STAGE, blocked_penalty, stage_index, item.get("id", ""))
   178→
   179→    # Workflow action items (e.g. create-plan)
   180→    if kind == "workflow_action":
   181→        return (_RANK_WORKFLOW, 0, 0, item.get("id", ""))
   182→
   183→    if kind == "cluster":
   184→        # Clusters sort before individual issues, ordered by action type
   185→        action_pri = ACTION_TYPE_PRIORITY.get(
   186→            item.get("action_type", "manual_fix"), 3
   187→        )
   188→        return (
   189→            _RANK_CLUSTER,
   190→            action_pri,
   191→            -int(item.get("member_count", 0)),
   192→            item.get("id", ""),
   193→        )
   194→
   195→    impact = item.get("estimated_impact", 0.0)
   196→
   197→    if kind == "subjective_dimension" or item.get("is_subjective"):
   198→        return (
   199→            _RANK_FINDING,
   200→            -impact,
   201→            subjective_score_value(item),
   202→            item.get("id", ""),
   203→        )
   204→
   205→    detail = detail_dict(item)
   206→    review_weight = float(item.get("review_weight", 0.0) or 0.0)
   207→    return (
   208→        _RANK_FINDING,
   209→        -impact,
   210→        CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(item.get("confidence", "low"), 9),
   211→        -review_weight,
   212→        -int(detail.get("count", 0) or 0),
   213→        item.get("id", ""),
   214→    )

   217→def item_sort_key(item: dict) -> tuple:
   218→    """Unified sort key: plan position first, then natural ranking.
   219→
   220→    When ``_plan_position`` is stamped (by :func:`stamp_plan_sort_keys`),
   221→    planned items sort first in plan order, then existing items by natural
   222→    ranking, then newly-discovered items by natural ranking.
   223→
   224→    When no plan fields are stamped, falls back to pure natural ranking.
   225→    """
   226→    plan_pos = item.get("_plan_position")
   227→
   228→    if plan_pos is not None:
   229→        kind = item.get("kind", "issue")
   230→        # Triage stages: even when explicitly planned, maintain the
   231→        # blocked-before-unblocked invariant for correctness.
   232→        if kind == "workflow_stage":
   233→            blocked = 1 if item.get("is_blocked") else 0
   234→            stage_idx = int(item.get("stage_index", 0))
   235→            return (_TIER_PLANNED, blocked, stage_idx, item.get("id", ""))
   236→        return (_TIER_PLANNED, 0, plan_pos, item.get("id", ""))
   237→
   238→    is_new = item.get("_is_new", False)
   239→    group = _TIER_NEW if is_new else _TIER_EXISTING
   240→    return (group, *_natural_sort_key(item))
   241→

   323→def group_queue_items(items: list[dict], group: str) -> dict[str, list[dict]]:
   324→    """Group queue items for alternate output modes."""
   325→    grouped: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
   326→    for item in items:
   327→        if group == "file":
   328→            key = item.get("file", "")
   329→        elif group == "detector":
   330→            key = item.get("detector", "")
   331→        elif group == "cluster":
   332→            plan_cluster = item.get("plan_cluster")
   333→            key = plan_cluster["name"] if isinstance(plan_cluster, dict) else "(unclustered)"
   334→        else:
   335→            key = "items"
   336→        grouped.setdefault(key, []).append(item)
   337→    return grouped
   338→

1→"""State-backed work queue for review issues.
     2→
     3→Review issues live in state["issues"]. This module provides:
     4→- Listing/sorting open review issues by impact
     5→- Storing investigation notes on issues
     6→- Expiring stale holistic issues during scan
     7→"""
     8→
     9→from __future__ import annotations
    10→
    11→import logging
    12→from datetime import UTC, datetime
    13→
    14→from desloppify.core.issues_render import issue_weight
    15→from desloppify.engine._work_queue.helpers import detail_dict
    16→
    17→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    18→
    19→__all__ = [
    20→    "impact_label",
    21→    "list_open_review_issues",
    22→    "update_investigation",
    23→    "expire_stale_holistic",
    24→]
    25→
    26→
    27→def impact_label(weight: float) -> str:
    28→    """Convert weight to a human-readable impact label."""
    29→    try:
    30→        numeric = float(weight)
    31→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
    32→        return "+"
    33→    if numeric >= 8:
    34→        return "+++"
    35→    if numeric >= 5:
    36→        return "++"
    37→    return "+"
    38→
    39→
    40→def list_open_review_issues(state: dict) -> list[dict]:
    41→    """Return open review issues sorted by impact (highest first)."""
    42→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
    43→    review = [
    44→        issue
    45→        for issue in issues.values()
    46→        if issue.get("status") == "open" and issue.get("detector") == "review"
    47→    ]
    48→
    49→    def _sort_key(issue: dict) -> tuple[float, str]:
    50→        weight, _impact, issue_id = issue_weight(issue)
    51→        return (-weight, issue_id)
    52→
    53→    review.sort(key=_sort_key)
    54→    return review
    55→
    56→
    57→def update_investigation(state: dict, issue_id: str, text: str) -> bool:
    58→    """Store investigation text on a issue. Returns False if not found/not open."""
    59→    issue = state.get("issues", {}).get(issue_id)
    60→    if not issue or issue.get("status") != "open":
    61→        return False
    62→    detail = detail_dict(issue)
    63→    if not detail:
    64→        detail = {}
    65→        issue["detail"] = detail
    66→    detail["investigation"] = text
    67→    detail["investigated_at"] = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
    68→    return True
    69→
    70→
    71→def expire_stale_holistic(state: dict, max_age_days: int = 30) -> list[str]:
    72→    """Auto-resolve holistic review issues older than max_age_days."""
    73→    now = datetime.now(UTC)
    74→    expired: list[str] = []
    75→
    76→    for issue_id, issue in state.get("issues", {}).items():
    77→        if issue.get("detector") != "review":
    78→            continue
    79→        if issue.get("status") != "open":
    80→            continue
    81→        if not detail_dict(issue).get("holistic"):
    82→            continue
    83→
    84→        last_seen = issue.get("last_seen")
    85→        if not last_seen:
    86→            continue
    87→
    88→        try:
    89→            seen_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(last_seen)
    90→        except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
    91→            logger.debug(
    92→                "Skipping holistic issue %s with invalid last_seen %r: %s",
    93→                issue_id,
    94→                last_seen,
    95→                exc,
    96→            )
    97→            continue
    98→
    99→        age_days = (now - seen_dt).days
   100→        if age_days > max_age_days:
   101→            issue["status"] = "auto_resolved"
   102→            issue["resolved_at"] = now.isoformat()
   103→            issue["note"] = "holistic review expired — re-run review to re-evaluate"
   104→            expired.append(issue_id)
   105→
   106→    return expired
   107→

1→"""Auto-resolution helpers for review re-import workflows."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from collections.abc import Callable
     6→from typing import Any
     7→
     8→from desloppify.state import utc_now
     9→
    10→
    11→def auto_resolve_review_issues(
    12→    state: dict[str, Any],
    13→    *,
    14→    new_ids: set[str],
    15→    diff: dict[str, Any],
    16→    note: str,
    17→    should_resolve: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], bool],
    18→    utc_now_fn=utc_now,
    19→) -> None:
    20→    """Auto-resolve stale open review issues that match a scope predicate."""
    21→    diff.setdefault("auto_resolved", 0)
    22→    for issue_id, issue in state.get("issues", {}).items():
    23→        if issue_id in new_ids or issue.get("status") != "open":
    24→            continue
    25→        if not should_resolve(issue):
    26→            continue
    27→        issue["status"] = "auto_resolved"
    28→        issue["resolved_at"] = utc_now_fn()
    29→        issue["note"] = note
    30→        diff["auto_resolved"] += 1
    31→

    72→def _validate_and_build_issues(
    73→    findings_list: list[ReviewIssuePayload],
    74→    holistic_prompts: dict[str, Any],
    75→    lang_name: str,
    76→) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], list[dict[str, Any]], list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    77→    """Validate raw holistic issues and build state-ready issue dicts.
    78→
    79→    Returns (review_issues, skipped, dismissed_concerns).
    80→    """
    81→    review_issues: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    82→    skipped: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    83→    dismissed_concerns: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    84→    allowed_dimensions = {
    85→        dim for dim in holistic_prompts if isinstance(dim, str) and dim.strip()
    86→    }
    87→
    88→    for idx, raw_finding in enumerate(findings_list):
    89→        issue, finding_errors = validate_review_finding_payload(
    90→            raw_finding,
    91→            label=f"issues[{idx}]",
    92→            allowed_dimensions=allowed_dimensions,
    93→            allow_dismissed=True,
    94→        )
    95→        if finding_errors:
    96→            skipped.append(
    97→                {
    98→                    "index": idx,
    99→                    "missing": finding_errors,
   100→                    "identifier": (
   101→                        raw_finding.get("identifier", "<none>")
   102→                        if isinstance(raw_finding, dict)
   103→                        else "<none>"
   104→                    ),
   105→                }
   106→            )
   107→            continue
   108→        assert issue is not None
   109→
   110→        # Handle dismissed concern verdicts (no dimension/summary required).
   111→        if issue.get("concern_verdict") == "dismissed":
   112→            fp = issue.get("concern_fingerprint", "")
   113→            if fp:
   114→                dismissed_concerns.append(
   115→                    {
   116→                        "fingerprint": fp,
   117→                        "concern_type": issue.get("concern_type", ""),
   118→                        "concern_file": issue.get("concern_file", ""),
   119→                        "reasoning": issue.get("reasoning", ""),
   120→                    }
   121→                )
   122→            continue
   123→
   124→        # Safety net: skip positive observations that slipped past the prompt.
   125→        summary_text = str(issue.get("summary", ""))
   126→        if summary_text.lower().startswith(_POSITIVE_PREFIXES):
   127→            skipped.append(
   128→                {
   129→                    "index": idx,
   130→                    "missing": ["positive observation (not a defect)"],
   131→                    "identifier": issue.get("identifier", "<none>"),
   132→                }
   133→            )
   134→            continue
   135→
   136→        dimension = issue["dimension"]
   137→
   138→        # Confirmed concern verdicts become "concerns" detector issues.
   139→        is_confirmed_concern = issue.get("concern_verdict") == "confirmed"
   140→        detector = "concerns" if is_confirmed_concern else "review"
   141→
   142→        content_hash = hashlib.sha256(summary_text.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
   143→        detail: dict[str, Any] = {
   144→            "holistic": True,
   145→            "dimension": dimension,
   146→            "related_files": issue["related_files"],
   147→            "evidence": issue["evidence"],
   148→            "suggestion": issue.get("suggestion", ""),
   149→            "reasoning": issue.get("reasoning", ""),
   150→        }
   151→        if is_confirmed_concern:
   152→            detail["concern_type"] = issue.get("concern_type", "")
   153→            detail["concern_verdict"] = "confirmed"
   154→
   155→        prefix = "concern" if is_confirmed_concern else "holistic"
   156→        file = issue.get("concern_file", "") if is_confirmed_concern else ""
   157→        confidence = normalize_review_confidence(issue.get("confidence", "low"))
   158→        imported = make_issue(
   159→            detector=detector,
   160→            file=file,
   161→            name=f"{prefix}::{dimension}::{issue['identifier']}::{content_hash}",
   162→            tier=review_tier(confidence, holistic=True),
   163→            confidence=confidence,
   164→            summary=summary_text,
   165→            detail=detail,
   166→        )
   167→        imported["lang"] = lang_name
   168→        review_issues.append(imported)
   169→
   170→    return review_issues, skipped, dismissed_concerns

   173→def _collect_imported_dimensions(
   174→    *,
   175→    findings_list: list[ReviewIssuePayload],
   176→    review_issues: list[dict[str, Any]],
   177→    assessments: dict[str, Any] | None,
   178→    review_scope: ReviewScopePayload | dict[str, Any] | None,
   179→    valid_dimensions: set[str],
   180→) -> set[str]:
   181→    """Return normalized dimensions this import explicitly covered."""
   182→    imported_dimensions: set[str] = set()
   183→
   184→    if isinstance(review_scope, dict):
   185→        scope_dims = review_scope.get("imported_dimensions")
   186→        if isinstance(scope_dims, list):
   187→            for raw_dim in scope_dims:
   188→                normalized = normalize_dimension_name(str(raw_dim))
   189→                if normalized in valid_dimensions:
   190→                    imported_dimensions.add(normalized)
   191→
   192→    for issue in findings_list:
   193→        if not isinstance(issue, dict):
   194→            continue
   195→        normalized = normalize_dimension_name(str(issue.get("dimension", "")))
   196→        if normalized in valid_dimensions:
   197→            imported_dimensions.add(normalized)
   198→
   199→    for issue in review_issues:
   200→        detail = issue.get("detail")
   201→        if not isinstance(detail, dict):
   202→            continue
   203→        normalized = normalize_dimension_name(str(detail.get("dimension", "")))
   204→        if normalized in valid_dimensions:
   205→            imported_dimensions.add(normalized)
   206→
   207→    for raw_dim in (assessments or {}):
   208→        normalized = normalize_dimension_name(str(raw_dim))
   209→        if normalized in valid_dimensions:
   210→            imported_dimensions.add(normalized)
   211→
   212→    return imported_dimensions
   213→
   214→
   215→def _auto_resolve_stale_holistic(
   216→    state: dict[str, Any],
   217→    new_ids: set[str],
   218→    diff: dict[str, Any],
   219→    utc_now_fn,
   220→    *,
   221→    imported_dimensions: set[str] | None = None,
   222→    full_sweep_included: bool | None = None,
   223→) -> None:
   224→    """Auto-resolve open holistic issues not present in the latest import."""
   225→    scope_dimensions = {
   226→        normalize_dimension_name(dim)
   227→        for dim in (imported_dimensions or set())
   228→        if isinstance(dim, str) and dim.strip()
   229→    }
   230→    scoped_reimport = full_sweep_included is False
   231→    # Partial re-import with unknown dimension scope: do not auto-resolve.
   232→    if scoped_reimport and not scope_dimensions:
   233→        return
   234→
   235→    def _should_resolve(issue: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
   236→        if issue.get("detector") not in ("review", "concerns"):
   237→            return False
   238→        detail = issue.get("detail")
   239→        if not isinstance(detail, dict) or not detail.get("holistic"):
   240→            return False
   241→        if not scoped_reimport:
   242→            return True
   243→        dimension = normalize_dimension_name(str(detail.get("dimension", "")))
   244→        return dimension in scope_dimensions
   245→
   246→    auto_resolve_review_issues(
   247→        state,
   248→        new_ids=new_ids,
   249→        diff=diff,
   250→        note="not reported in latest holistic re-import",
   251→        should_resolve=_should_resolve,
   252→        utc_now_fn=utc_now_fn,
   253→    )

   255→
   256→def import_holistic_issues(
   257→    issues_data: ReviewImportPayload,
   258→    state: dict[str, Any],
   259→    lang_name: str,
   260→    *,
   261→    project_root: Path | str | None = None,
   262→    utc_now_fn=utc_now,
   263→) -> dict[str, Any]:
   264→    """Import holistic (codebase-wide) issues into state."""
   265→    payload: ReviewImportEnvelope = parse_review_import_payload(
   266→        issues_data,
   267→        mode_name="Holistic",
   268→    )
   269→    findings_list = payload.issues
   270→    assessments = payload.assessments
   271→    reviewed_files = payload.reviewed_files
   272→    review_scope = issues_data.get("review_scope", {})
   273→    if not isinstance(review_scope, dict):
   274→        review_scope = {}
   275→    review_scope.setdefault("full_sweep_included", None)
   276→    scope_full_sweep = review_scope.get("full_sweep_included")
   277→    if not isinstance(scope_full_sweep, bool):
   278→        scope_full_sweep = None
   279→    if assessments:
   280→        store_assessments(
   281→            state,
   282→            assessments,
   283→            source="holistic",
   284→            utc_now_fn=utc_now_fn,
   285→        )
   286→
   287→    _, holistic_prompts, _ = load_dimensions_for_lang(lang_name)
   288→    valid_dimensions = {
   289→        normalize_dimension_name(dim)
   290→        for dim in holistic_prompts
   291→        if isinstance(dim, str)
   292→    }
   293→    review_issues, skipped, dismissed_concerns = _validate_and_build_issues(
   294→        findings_list, holistic_prompts, lang_name
   295→    )
   296→    imported_dimensions = _collect_imported_dimensions(
   297→        findings_list=findings_list,
   298→        review_issues=review_issues,
   299→        assessments=assessments if isinstance(assessments, dict) else None,
   300→        review_scope=review_scope,
   301→        valid_dimensions=valid_dimensions,
   302→    )
   303→
   304→    # Store dismissed concern verdicts for suppression in future concern generation.
   305→    if dismissed_concerns:
   306→        from desloppify.engine.concerns import generate_concerns
   307→
   308→        store = state.setdefault("concern_dismissals", {})
   309→        now = utc_now_fn()
   310→        # Compute current concerns to get source_finding_ids for each fingerprint.
   311→        current_concerns = generate_concerns(state, lang_name=lang_name)
   312→        concern_sources = {
   313→            c.fingerprint: list(c.source_issues) for c in current_concerns
   314→        }
   315→        for dc in dismissed_concerns:
   316→            fp = dc["fingerprint"]
   317→            store[fp] = {
   318→                "dismissed_at": now,
   319→                "reasoning": dc.get("reasoning", ""),
   320→                "concern_type": dc.get("concern_type", ""),
   321→                "concern_file": dc.get("concern_file", ""),
   322→                "source_finding_ids": concern_sources.get(fp, []),
   323→            }
   324→
   325→    potentials = _lang_potentials(state, lang_name)
   326→    existing_review = potentials.get("review", 0)
   327→    potentials["review"] = max(existing_review, HOLISTIC_POTENTIAL)
   328→
   329→    concern_count = sum(1 for f in review_issues if f.get("detector") == "concerns")
   330→    if concern_count:
   331→        potentials["concerns"] = max(potentials.get("concerns", 0), concern_count)
   332→
   333→    merge_potentials_dict: dict[str, int] = {"review": potentials.get("review", 0)}
   334→    if potentials.get("concerns", 0) > 0:
   335→        merge_potentials_dict["concerns"] = potentials["concerns"]
   336→
   337→    diff = merge_scan(
   338→        state,
   339→        review_issues,
   340→        options=MergeScanOptions(
   341→            lang=lang_name,
   342→            potentials=merge_potentials_dict,
   343→            merge_potentials=True,
   344→        ),
   345→    )
   346→
   347→    new_ids = {issue["id"] for issue in review_issues}
   348→    _auto_resolve_stale_holistic(
   349→        state,
   350→        new_ids,
   351→        diff,
   352→        utc_now_fn,
   353→        imported_dimensions=imported_dimensions,
   354→        full_sweep_included=scope_full_sweep,
   355→    )
   356→
   357→    if skipped:
   358→        diff["skipped"] = len(skipped)
   359→        diff["skipped_details"] = skipped
   360→
   361→    update_reviewed_file_cache(
   362→        state,
   363→        reviewed_files,
   364→        project_root=project_root,
   365→        utc_now_fn=utc_now_fn,
   366→    )
   367→    resolve_reviewed_file_coverage_issues(
   368→        state,
   369→        diff,
   370→        reviewed_files,
   371→        utc_now_fn=utc_now_fn,
   372→    )
   373→    update_holistic_review_cache(
   374→        state,
   375→        findings_list,
   376→        lang_name=lang_name,
   377→        review_scope=review_scope,
   378→        utc_now_fn=utc_now_fn,
   379→    )
   380→    resolve_holistic_coverage_issues(state, diff, utc_now_fn=utc_now_fn)
   381→
   382→    # Clean up dismissals whose source issues were all resolved — runs after
   383→    # all issue mutations (merge_scan, auto_resolve, coverage resolve) so it
   384→    # sees the final state.
   385→    from desloppify.engine.concerns import cleanup_stale_dismissals
   386→
   387→    cleanup_stale_dismissals(state)
   388→
   389→    return diff

   392→def _resolve_total_files(state: dict[str, Any], lang_name: str | None) -> int:
   393→    """Best-effort total file count from codebase_metrics or review cache."""
   394→    review_cache = state.get("review_cache", {})
   395→    fallback = len(review_cache.get("files", {}))
   396→
   397→    codebase_metrics = state.get("codebase_metrics", {})
   398→    if not isinstance(codebase_metrics, dict):
   399→        return fallback
   400→
   401→    # Try language-specific metrics first, then global.
   402→    sources = []
   403→    if lang_name:
   404→        lang_metrics = codebase_metrics.get(lang_name)
   405→        if isinstance(lang_metrics, dict):
   406→            sources.append(lang_metrics)
   407→    sources.append(codebase_metrics)
   408→
   409→    for source in sources:
   410→        metric_total = source.get("total_files")
   411→        if isinstance(metric_total, int) and metric_total > 0:
   412→            return metric_total
   413→
   414→    return fallback
   415→

   417→def update_holistic_review_cache(
   418→    state: dict[str, Any],
   419→    issues_data: list[dict],
   420→    *,
   421→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   422→    review_scope: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   423→    utc_now_fn=utc_now,

   425→    """Store holistic review metadata in review_cache."""
   426→    review_cache = state.setdefault("review_cache", {})
   427→    now = utc_now_fn()
   428→    _, holistic_prompts, _ = load_dimensions_for_lang(lang_name or "")
   429→
   430→    valid = [
   431→        issue
   432→        for issue in issues_data
   433→        if all(
   434→            key in issue
   435→            for key in ("dimension", "identifier", "summary", "confidence")
   436→        )
   437→        and issue["dimension"] in holistic_prompts

   439→
   440→    resolved_total_files: int
   441→    total_override = (
   442→        review_scope.get("total_files")

   444→        else None
   445→    )
   446→    if (
   447→        isinstance(total_override, int)
   448→        and not isinstance(total_override, bool)

   475→def resolve_holistic_coverage_issues(
   476→    state: dict[str, Any],
   477→    diff: dict[str, Any],
   478→    *,
   479→    utc_now_fn=utc_now,
   480→) -> None:
   481→    """Resolve stale holistic coverage entries after successful holistic import."""
   482→    now = utc_now_fn()
   483→    for issue in state.get("issues", {}).values():
   484→        if issue.get("status") != "open":
   485→            continue
   486→        if issue.get("detector") != "subjective_review":

   489→        issue_id = issue.get("id", "")

   496→        issue["status"] = "auto_resolved"
   497→        issue["resolved_at"] = now
   498→        issue["note"] = "resolved by holistic review import"
   499→        issue["resolution_attestation"] = {

   502→            "attested_at": now,
   503→            "scan_verified": False,
   504→        }

   508→def resolve_reviewed_file_coverage_issues(

   534→        finding_file = issue.get("file", "")

     3→from __future__ import annotations

     5→import logging

    13→def get_file_issues(state: dict, filepath: str) -> list[dict]:
    14→    """Get existing open issues for a file (summaries for context)."""
    15→    rpath = rel(filepath)
    16→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
    17→    return [
    18→        {"detector": issue["detector"], "summary": issue["summary"], "id": issue["id"]}
    19→        for issue in issues.values()
    20→        if issue.get("file") == rpath and issue["status"] == "open"
    21→    ]
    22→
    23→
    24→def count_fresh(state: dict, max_age_days: int) -> int:
    25→    """Count files in review cache that are still fresh."""
    26→    cache = state.get("review_cache", {}).get("files", {})
    27→    now = datetime.now(UTC)
    28→    count = 0
    29→    for entry in cache.values():
    30→        reviewed_at = entry.get("reviewed_at", "")
    31→        if reviewed_at:
    32→            try:
    33→                reviewed = datetime.fromisoformat(reviewed_at)
    34→                if (now - reviewed).days <= max_age_days:
    35→                    count += 1
    36→            except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
    37→                logger.debug(
    38→                    "Invalid review cache date %r while counting fresh files: %s",
    39→                    reviewed_at,
    40→                    exc,
    41→                )
    42→    return count
    43→
    44→
    45→def count_stale(state: dict, max_age_days: int) -> int:
    46→    """Count files in review cache that are stale."""
    47→    cache = state.get("review_cache", {}).get("files", {})
    48→    total = len(cache)
    49→    return total - count_fresh(state, max_age_days)
    50→
    51→
    52→__all__ = ["count_fresh", "count_stale", "get_file_issues"]
    53→
    54→
